chapter: Cotton Club and radio fame with Cab
title: How bands made singers: Sinatra and Bing Crosby
summary: Thomas says bands made more singers than anyone; he credits Tommy Dorsey for Sinatra's phrasing and idolizes Bing Crosby, whose records he bought.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Because bands made singers... Probably Frank Sinatra.

Because I knew a musician that knew the band that did the audition for the club-owner, I think it must have been the Rusty Cabin, and the man that had the Rusty Cabin said, 'I'll take the band, but I don't want that singer.' And the guys were so together, they wouldn't take the job unless they took Frank Sinatra. Then Frank Sinatra got involved with the trombone player. And I actually think... Somebody just said of (?) who he gives credit for his style. But Frank Sinatra copied his style after Tommy Dorsey. Because he holds...
Well, that's the band he made his big hit with, 'I'll Never Smile Again.'

Yeah. Because he copied the... He's the greatest phraser, in my estimation, of any of them. He can play the song better than anybody. Because you know, we had a song from the Cotton Club we never got popular playing, but Frank Sinatra made a hit out of it -- "World On A String." And even to this day, he can style a song. Of course, my idol was Bing Crosby.
I used to buy every record he made, everything he put out. I didn't ask to hear the record. I'd just say, 'What's the latest thing on Bing Crosby?'

Do you remember when we used to have in Cab's band, we used to have between shows... We used to have a Bing Crosby concert, when we'd just bought the Bing Crosby records. I'm happy to sit here and tell you that I made the last record with him that he ever made.
He was such a great guy.
One of the most beautiful human beings I've ever known. But go on.

It was such a pleasure playing that time with him at the Paramount. Because I've got an autographed picture right now that he autographed. And he looked so different. I often... When I knew you was going on a tour with him, I wanted you to take the picture and show it to

him, because he'd have got a kick out of it.
So the Cotton Club went downtown. So then, we got in the mainstream.
